p.IMAGESET-DECLARED-FRAMES: **A declared frame set replaces the frames the shipped file carries.** `frames` lists the sizes of the frames the target is written with - square frames, a size each, in the order the written file carries them - and may add frames the shipped file lacks and drop frames it carries. What such a list may be is a question of the container, so the engine asks the codec of the target's container (the member `declaredFrames` of `ImageCodec`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-BRAND-IMAGES`) and names no container itself: the codec answers the frames a write carries, or the reason it refuses the list, and the engine turns the reason into `CK-E-CONFIG`. A container whose codec answers no frame set refuses every declared frame set of its targets - `a declared frame set is not supported for a target of the <kind> container` - so a declaration is never silently ignored. The run renders exactly the declared frames, each from its own master (`##IMAGESET-MASTERS`, `##IMAGESET-DECLARED-SOURCES`), and the container is written from them in the declared order by the codec's ordinary writer; which lists a container takes and how its writer encodes a frame it adds is the answer of the type (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-006#IMAGESET-ICO-FRAME-SET`). The dry run, the index and the verification take the same frames. A target the declaration does not name, or names with `sources` alone, keeps the frames of its shipped file (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-006#IMAGESET-TARGET-DISCOVERY`), and a patch set that declares nothing gets every file `gen` writes byte for byte as before declarations existed: a test pins the sha256 of every file of two runs over the fixture - a seeded one and one from vector, raster, per-size and 16-bit masters of the whole brand surface - to what the generator wrote before this fact.

p.IMAGESET-DECLARED-SOURCES: **A declared source gives some frames of a target to another master key.** A rule of `sources` names a `key` and selects frames by their size - an NxN frame has the size N, and a frame that is not square is never selected - with exactly one selector: `sizes`, the explicit list, or `minSize` and `maxSize`, an inclusive range with at least one bound. The rules apply to the frames of the target once `frames` has been applied - the declared ones or the shipped ones - and a frame no rule selects keeps the target's own key (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-006#IMAGESET-ARTWORK`). A key is written like any key, one segment or `<family>/<artwork>`, of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, no segment starting with `.`; its masters follow the one naming convention and precedence of `##IMAGESET-MASTERS` - `<key>-<N>.png` over `<key>.svg` over `<key>.png` - and are reported like the masters of any key, the stretch (`##IMAGESET-STRETCH-REPORTED`) and the 16-bit reduction (`##IMAGESET-SELF-CHECK-READS-MASTERS`) included; a frame its key has no master for skips the target the usual way. `CK-E-CONFIG` refuses, with no fallback: a key none of whose masters exists in the directory; overlapping rules - one frame selected by two rules, whatever their keys - and contradicting ones - `sizes` together with a range, a `minSize` greater than its `maxSize`, a size listed twice; and a selector that matches no frame - a listed size that is not a frame of the target, a range that selects none. The frames of `resources/win32/code.ico` up to 64 px from the key `taskbar` - `taskbar.svg`, `taskbar-16.png`, `taskbar-32.png` - are the rule `{"key": "taskbar", "maxSize": 64}`.

p.IMAGESET-FRAME-SOURCES-REPORTED: **Every report says where each frame came from.** `gen` and `gen --dry-run` state per frame, as before, the size, the master file and how it was used - `override <file> verbatim`, `rendered <file>`, `resampled <file>` - with the stretch and the 16-bit reduction, the file naming its key by the naming convention; a frame a rule of the declaration gave to its key adds `, from the declared key <key>`, and the line of the dry run that opens a target with a declared frame set adds `, declared in imageset.json in place of the shipped <sizes>`. Under `--json` every frame of `data.targets[].frames[]` also carries `key`, `keyDeclared`, `master` and `origin` (`override`, `vector` or `raster`), and every target `framesDeclared`. `imageset index` records the declaration: a target with a declared frame set has the line `- Frames: declared in imageset.json - <sizes>; the shipped file carries <sizes>`, the From column of a size a rule gave to its key adds `, from the declared key <key>`, and the section of the masters names the declaration; under `--json` every size of `data.targets[].sizes[]` carries `key`, `keyDeclared` and `origin` beside `from` - `origin` null where no master serves the size - every target `framesDeclared` and `shippedFrames`, and `data.declaration` names the file. The text about a target nothing declares does not change; its JSON carries the same fields, with the target's own key, `keyDeclared: false` and `framesDeclared: false`.

p.IMAGESET-VERIFY-DECLARED: **`imageset verify` checks a declared target against its declaration and never compares two keys.** It reads the declaration of the masters directory it is pointed at and validates it as `gen` does (`##IMAGESET-DECLARATION`); the masters still take no part in any measurement. The layers of a target are grouped by the master key that serves them, and each group has its own round trip: regenerated from its own largest layer - the first in file order on a tie - and compared within the bands (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION`). A layer of one key is never compared with a layer of another, because two keys are two drawings for the same reason two containers are (`##IMAGESET-ROUND-TRIP`). A group of one layer has nothing to regenerate it from and says so - `the only layer of key <key> in this file, so nothing here regenerates it` - and is no comparison. For a target with a declared frame set the structure of the file in the tree is compared with the declaration, not with the frames the pin shipped: a frame the declaration lists and the file lacks, a frame the file carries and the declaration does not list, or another order, is a structural mismatch - the gate, exit 1 - and the report names the missing and the extra frames. The drift the gate catches is therefore a missing frame, an extra frame, and a frame drawn from the wrong key wherever the group of its key asserts a band - at 64 px and above, in a group of more than one layer; below 64 px no pixel criterion is asserted at all, so there such a frame is measured and printed, not failed. Under `--json` every layer carries its `key`, every target `framesDeclared` and `masters` - one `{key, label}` per group - and `structure` also `declared`, `missing` and `extra`; `data.declaration` names the file, and the summary says the targets were verified against it. A target nothing declares is verified, and reported in the text, exactly as before.

p.IMAGESET-ROUND-TRIP: The acceptance criterion is a round trip on the distribution's own artifact: take the largest image of the distribution as the master, regenerate, and compare with the shipped one. The structure EXACTLY: the same container type, the same list of frames/types, the same sizes, in the order of the file; this is asserted by a test against the shipped binary (not against a file the test has just written), and a mutation of the encoder must turn the test red. The pixels do not have to match at the small sizes: the small layers upstream are drawn separately rather than obtained by reduction; the tolerance is set by size ranges and is justified by the worker's own measurement, not by a reference to somebody else's figure. The worker's own measurement on the upstream tree (the master is the largest layer of THE SAME container - `.icns` must not be compared with `.ico`, they are different drawings: mean alpha 158.7/255 against 219.1/255): the mean absolute RGB channel difference against the shipped layer is 1.0/255 at 512x512 and 2.3/255 at 256x256 (`code.icns` from `ic10` 1024), 4.7/255 at 128x128 (`code.icns`), 13.1/255 at 128x128 (`code.ico` from its own 256 frame), 17.9/255 and 20.2/255 at 32x32 (`code.ico` and `code.icns`) and 65.6/255 at 16x16 (`code.ico`). Hence the tolerance by ranges - `##DECISION-IMAGESET-ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION`. The cross-container difference was measured twice and the two results diverged (96.5 against 130.9); the analysis of 2026-09-06 showed that the honest figure is **96.5/255**: it is the same MAE over the three RGB channels on raw buffers as every other row of the table, computed between the shipped 256x256 frame of `code.ico` and the shipped `ic13` element of `code.icns`, without resampling on either side. An exhaustive sweep of frame×element pairs gives a range of 94.8–102.9 by this metric, so 130.9 is unreachable by it on any pair: it is a quantity of the RMS family (a global RMSE over RGBA gives 131.1, and `magick compare -metric RMSE` reports the same), and it has no place in a table of mean absolute differences. The share of fully transparent pixels says more than any of these figures: **32.6% for `ic13` against 14.1% for the 256x256 frame of the `.ico`** - that is exactly the rounded macOS margin, and it must not be confused with the MAE.

p.IMAGESET-NO-TOOLS: `codkit imageset --help` must answer honestly the question "which tools have to be installed": with this construction the answer is "none, on every supported OS", and it is printed plainly, with the list of the linked libraries and their licences (the npm closure: `@resvg/resvg-js` and its platform binaries - MPL-2.0; the statically linked crates: resvg/usvg - MPL-2.0, tiny-skia - BSD-3-Clause, rustybuzz/ttf-parser/roxmltree/svgtypes/simplecss/fontdb/data-url/xmlwriter/png/flate2/serde_json - Apache-2.0 OR MIT, zlib - Zlib), so that the reader can check the claim rather than believe it. Inventing a list of "optional tools" for the look of it is forbidden. The licence scan must cover the closure of the dependencies and not the top-level package, and its output is recorded in the report; there is no GPL/LGPL/AGPL in the closure in any form.

p.IMAGESET-NAMESPACE: `imageset` is a namespace, not a command with flags. The verbs: `imageset gen` (`##CMD-IMAGESET`), `imageset index` (`##IMAGESET-INDEX`) and `imageset verify` (`##IMAGESET-VERIFY`). A bare `codkit imageset` without a subcommand, and `codkit imageset <unknown>`, print the list of subcommands and exit 2 - by the same `usageFail` path an unknown command answers through, and BEFORE any root is resolved; no work at all is done. The name is resolved by the existing longest-match mechanism of `main.ts` (`MAX_COMMAND_WORDS`), the same one `marker new`, `overlay apply|check` and `build up|down|status|errors` use. The exception is `codkit imageset --help`: the one flag of the namespace, it prints the long help and the list of subcommands (`##IMAGESET-NO-TOOLS`), exit 0.

p.IMAGESET-INDEX: `codkit imageset index [--branding-dir path]` is read-only: an index of the icon set computed from the same two sources `gen` uses (the targets of the distribution and the masters directory), so it reports the discovered state and cannot go stale (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-INDEX-IS-COMPUTED`). It writes nothing, seeding included: the index of an unseeded directory reports `missing` for every size and names the command that seeds. It takes no lock (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-INDEX-NO-LOCK`). Per target: the path in the tree and the **role** - where a human sees the image (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-ROLE-TABLE`); the container type and the exact list of required sizes/types discovered from the distribution, or declared by the product (`##IMAGESET-DECLARED-FRAMES`); per size the key and the file it comes from (`##IMAGESET-FRAME-SOURCES-REPORTED`) and its **source**: `master` (a master of exactly this size exists and is taken verbatim), `generated` (it will be rendered or resampled from a base master named by name) or `missing` (there is no master, the run will skip the target); and the constraints that come before drawing - whether transparency or an explicitly filled background is expected, that the master fills the frame without margins, and that a master of the exact size whose dimensions do not match drops the whole target. Once, the document states the rule that hand-made masters are preferred, together with the measurement that justifies it (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-PER-SIZE-MASTERS`). The output defaults to Markdown (the form handed to an agent); `--json` is the ordinary schema-2 envelope with the same data structurally, and both forms are rendered from ONE model and cannot diverge. Exit 0 no matter how many masters are missing: a missing master is information, not a refusal; a non-zero code is reserved for a real breakage (an unreadable tree, an unparsable container or a master `gen` would refuse - 2, `##IMAGESET-SELF-CHECK-READS-MASTERS`). Before the list of targets comes the summary by family (`## Families`: drawings, from a master, generated, missing) - on a set of eighty-odd targets it is what people read, while the per-target list remains for whoever came for a particular picture. **The reading of the criterion "a hand-made master appears - one row flips"** (owner's decision of 2026-09-06): one row means one row of the PER-SIZE table. The row of the masters inventory and the totals count that same flip and must change together with it - a total that does not change when the source changes would be a defect. The test pins the exact list of changed rows and not their number: a second flip hidden behind the totals must turn it red.

p.IMAGESET-ARTWORK: Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-006#IMAGESET-ARTWORK; the address stays for citations.

p.IMAGESET-SVG-PASSTHROUGH: Some of the brand images are loaded by the distribution as vectors (the empty-editor watermarks), and there is no point in rasterizing them: the master is the artifact, and regeneration is handing out its bytes without a single change. Exactly two things are checked, both so that a wrong master does not travel into the product silently: the master must be a vector (`<key>.svg`; a raster master on a vector target is an honest skip of the target with a named reason, not a silent resampling), and it must carry the nominal size the distribution ships (otherwise the watermark would slide about in the layout). There is no resampling, no palette, no background and no tolerance on this path at all: either the bytes are exactly the same, or the target is skipped. A consequence whoever draws has to know: the whole content of the master, the SVG comments included, reaches the sources of the product verbatim.

p.IMAGESET-VERIFY: `codkit imageset verify [--branding-dir path] [--json]` is the acceptance run of the tolerance bands (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION`) against the distribution the operator already has, and the one place where those bands become an executable gate (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-VERIFY-COMMAND`). For every raster target of the fork tree the largest layer of THAT SAME container is taken, the other layers are regenerated from it through the working pipeline, and each is compared with the shipped one: the structure exactly (the container type, the list of frames and elements, the sizes, the order of the file), the pixels within the bands. A comparison between containers is forbidden by construction: the master is always a layer of the same file, and no flag can go around it (`##IMAGESET-ROUND-TRIP` explains why a cross-container comparison measures different drawings). A target with exactly one layer (PNG, BMP, XPM, SVG) yields no round trip and is marked unverifiable - it is not counted as passed. A target of the product's declaration is verified against the declaration, one master key at a time (`##IMAGESET-VERIFY-DECLARED`). The command only reads: the fork tree is opened for reading, it takes no lock (the same argument as `##DECISION-IMAGESET-INDEX-NO-LOCK`), it writes nothing into patchset or into the masters directory, and it does not seed the masters directory. The report names, for every comparison, the target, the size, the band and the measured value - a figure has to be re-checkable, not taken on faith; `--json` carries the same data structurally, from the same model as the Markdown. Codes: 0 - every verifiable target is inside its band; 1 - at least one is outside, and that is the gate; 2 - the environment (no tree, an unparsable container).

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-RASTERISER:
**Decision:** the rasterizer is `@resvg/resvg-js` 2.6.2, and it is the only dependency the feature adds.
**Why:** The MPL-2.0 licence is inside the permitted set (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-PERMISSIVE-LICENCES`); zero runtime dependencies in the npm closure; twelve prebuilt platform binaries (darwin x64/arm64; linux x64/arm64/arm, each in gnu and musl; win32 x64/ia32/arm64; android), so nothing is installed onto the host and the `--help` answer to the question "which tools are needed" - "none, on every supported OS" - is checkable and not merely declared.
**Considered and rejected:** - `sharp` - it pulls in libvips under LGPL, which the licence rule forbids without discussion; - system tools (`icotool`, `iconutil`, ImageMagick) - platform-dependent, they require an installation and break the cross-platform property the prebuilt binaries were chosen for; - a pure-JS SVG rasterizer - no candidate covers the usvg profile, and a divergence in rendering would be discovered only on somebody else's machine.
**When to revisit:** if `@resvg/resvg-js` publishes no release for 24 months; or a platform codkit supports disappears from the set of its platform binaries (observed through the `optionalDependencies` list in `npm-shrinkwrap.json`); or its licence in the closure stops being MPL-2.0.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-CONTAINER-ENCODERS:
**Decision:** the ICO, ICNS, BMP, XPM and PNG codecs are hand-written inside codkit; there are no codec packages.
**Why:** The containers are trivial: ICO - a 6-byte header and 16 bytes per directory frame with a PNG payload, ICNS - `icns` plus the length and elements of `<type><length><PNG>`; all together that is ~800 lines in `packages/codkit/src/lib/imageset*.ts`. The result was checked not by our own parser but by other people's: `icotool -l` showed four frames 16/32/128/256 at 32 bits, `icns2png -l` showed every type at the right sizes and depth, plus Pillow independently.
**Considered and rejected:** - encoder packages (`png-to-ico`, `icns-lib`, `jimp`) - a dependency and a licence surface each, for a few dozen lines; - calling the system `icotool`/`iconutil` - platform-dependent, the same argument as in `##DECISION-IMAGESET-RASTERISER`.
**When to revisit:** if upstream puts into an `.ico` or an `.icns` an element that is not a PNG payload and has to be reproduced - observed through a non-empty `data.targets[].legacyTypes` for a type that stopped being legacy.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-NATIVE-SIZE-RENDER:
**Decision:** every size is rendered by the rasterizer at its own native resolution; there is no resampling in the vector path at all.
**Why:** This is exactly the reason no image-processing library is needed: the only resampler in the code is the Lanczos-3 for raster masters (`##IMAGESET-RASTER`), and it never takes part when the master is a vector. The price of the alternative has been measured: a reduction 256→16 gives a mean difference of 65.6/255 against the shipped layer (`##IMAGESET-ROUND-TRIP`), whereas a native render goes through the full usvg pipeline on the geometry of the target size.
**Considered and rejected:** - one big render followed by a reduction - it requires a resampler (and usually an image library as well) and loses quality at exactly the sizes where it matters most; - rendering at 2x and halving - the same resampler, only disguised as "supersampling".
**When to revisit:** if a full run of `codkit imageset gen` on a real distribution (20 targets, 30 required sizes by `imageset index`) becomes longer than 60 s by `time` - then reusing one render would start to pay for the loss of quality.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-PER-SIZE-MASTERS:
**Decision:** a hand-made master of the exact size (`<family>-<N>.png`) is used verbatim and beats any generation; generation is the fallback path, not the default.
**Why:** Measured on the distribution's own artwork (the upstream tree; the master is the largest layer of the same container): the mean absolute RGB channel difference against the shipped layer is 1.0/255 at 512x512, 2.3/255 at 256x256, 4.7/255 at 128x128 for `code.icns`, 13.1/255 at 128x128 for `code.ico`, 17.9–20.2/255 at 32x32 and 65.6/255 at 16x16. That is, the shipped 16x16 layer is not a reduction of a large one but a separately drawn, simplified mark: upstream itself draws the small sizes separately, and that is what forbids throwing the small masters away as "duplicates".
**Considered and rejected:** - always generate - measurably worse: 65.6/255 at 16x16 against 2.3/255 at 256x256, a difference of thirtyfold; - simplify the mark automatically on reduction - codkit does not know the semantics of the mark and would replace the designer's decision with a guess.
**When to revisit:** if the measurement at 16x16 (the round-trip script, the campaign report) drops below 10/255 - then generation becomes indistinguishable and separate masters stop being mandatory.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-RESOURCE-LAYER-DELIVER:
**Decision:** the result is delivered by the existing resource-file layer: the files in `delta/resources/files/`, the entries in `delta/resources/map.json`.
**Why:** `codkit load` already materializes this layer into the fork tree (PROP-005 §6), so not a line of new machinery is needed, and the product repository receives ordinary resource artifacts - nothing in them tells that `imageset` generated them. Checked e2e: `gen` writes `delta/resources/files/resources/win32/code.ico`, and the next `load` puts the byte-for-byte same file into the tree.
**Considered and rejected:** - a separate imageset layer - new machinery in `load`, `verify` and `inventory`, and it would leak into the product repository as an implementation detail; - writing straight into the fork tree - it bypasses patchset, and the next `load` would wipe the result out.
**When to revisit:** if the resource-file layer stops accepting binary targets, or its map gets a format incompatible with the `CK-brand-*` entries.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-DISCOVERED-TARGETS:
**Decision:** the structure of every target is read from the bytes of the distribution's file; only the list of paths and globs is fixed in the code.
**Why:** The upstream frame sets are irregular and they change: in the tree that was checked `code.ico` carries 4 frames (16/32/128/256), `code.icns` carries 8 PNG-capable elements plus the legacy `ic04`, `ic05`, `info`, and the installer graphics exist at seven scales with non-square sizes (`inno-small-125.bmp` - 64x68, `inno-small-225.bmp` - 119x123, `inno-big-250.bmp` - 410x797). In total, 20 targets and 30 required sizes. A hard-coded table would diverge from the tree silently - exactly the failure the command has to prevent.
**Considered and rejected:** - a table of sizes in the code - it goes stale silently and without a single signal; - reading the sizes from `product.json` or `build/` - they are not there, they would have to be put there and a second copy of the truth maintained.
**When to revisit:** if upstream moves off the fixed paths `resources/win32`, `resources/darwin`, `resources/linux` - observed through the line "target absent in the tree" in the output of `gen` and `index`.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION:
**Decision:** acceptance is exact structural equality with the shipped binary plus a tolerance by size ranges: 256 px and above - mean |ΔRGB| ≤ 10/255; 64–255 px - ≤ 25/255; **below 64 px** - no pixel criterion is asserted at all, only the structure is checked.
**Why:** The thresholds are taken from our own measurement with a twofold margin: the maximum measured at ≥256 is 2.3/255, at 64–128 it is 13.1/255, and at 32 and 16 it is 20.2/255 and 65.6/255 (`##IMAGESET-ROUND-TRIP`). A threshold that would always be red is one somebody will loosen - this project has already fallen that way; so at the small sizes the criterion is honestly absent, and its place is taken by `index`, which names by name the missing master of the exact size.
**Considered and rejected:** - pixel equality with the shipped file - unreachable (65.6/255 at 16x16), it would be red forever and then loosened; - one tolerance for every size - it either lets a regression at 512 through or is red forever at 16; - a structural test against a file the test has just written itself - it proves nothing: the comparison is with the shipped binary, and a mutation of the encoder must turn the test red.
**The boundary is 64, not 32.** The first edition said "32 px and below" and left 33–63 px without any rule at all: the implementation could assert nothing there, because there is not a single measurement of our own in that range, and a threshold from the neighboring band would have been carried over without a basis. The distribution does carry real frames in that range (20, 24, 48 px among the file-type icons), they are measured and printed in the report, but they do not count as acceptance - the hole in the rule is closed by an honest "not asserted" and not by a guess.
**When to revisit:** if the measurement in the ≥256 range exceeds 10/255, or in 64–255 exceeds 25/255 - the rasterizer or the resampler has changed, and the threshold is revisited together with the cause and not on its own; or when a measurement of our own appears at 33–63 px with which that band can be justified.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-NAMESPACE:
**Decision:** `imageset` is a namespace: generation lives in `imageset gen`, the report in `imageset index`, and a bare `codkit imageset` prints the list of subcommands and exits 2, doing nothing.
**Why:** The owner's direction of 2026-09-06. The mechanism is not new: `marker new`, `overlay apply|check` and `build up|down|status|errors` are already resolved by the longest match in `main.ts`, and the `imageset` subcommands are resolved by the same code. A root that generates "just in case" is exactly the dumping ground the split is made against.
**Considered and rejected:** - one command with flags (`--index`) - the root becomes a dumping ground as the verbs appear; - the bare root as a synonym for `gen` - it silently does work where a human asked for help, and that is exactly the failure that is forbidden.
**When to revisit:** if `imageset` is left with one subcommand - observed through the number of definitions prefixed `imageset ` in the `COMMANDS` map (`packages/codkit/src/main.ts`).

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-SEEDING:
**Decision:** a missing masters directory is not an error: the first `gen` creates it and fills it with the distribution's own artwork from the fork tree; an existing directory is never overwritten.
**Why:** The owner's direction. And it is what makes the round trip meaningful on the very first day: the operator starts from real upstream material and replaces it piece by piece. Checked e2e: the first `gen` seeds `icon.png`, `installer-big.png` and `installer-small.png` and prints which file and which size each of them was taken from.
**Considered and rejected:** - treating the absence as an error - the operator has nowhere to take the first master from, and a first run becomes impossible; - topping up an existing directory - it would overwrite hand-made masters, that is, destroy exactly what is worth most.
**When to revisit:** if the distribution turns out to have no raster icon at all to seed from - observed through an empty `data.seeded` while the directory is absent.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-DEFAULT-MASTERS-DIR:
**Decision:** the masters live by default in `<patchset>/branding/`; `--branding-dir` exists only to override that, and a run without the flag has to work.
**Why:** The owner's direction. The path is derived from the root of the product repository, which codkit resolves anyway (`--patches-dir`, the environment variable, the settings file), so no new configuration appears, and the masters are versioned by the same commit as the delta they produce.
**Considered and rejected:** - requiring the flag on every run - the run stops being reproducible from memory; - a key in `codkit.json` - one more configuration field for a value that is unambiguously derived from the root.
**When to revisit:** if more than one set of masters is needed in one patchset (a separate dark mark, for instance) - then the default has to become a list rather than one path.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-INDEX-IS-COMPUTED:
**Decision:** `index` computes the report on every run from the targets of the distribution and the masters directory; there is no static document about the icon set in the repository.
**Why:** The two sources change independently: upstream changes the set of frames, the operator puts masters in and takes them out. One tree that was checked gives 20 targets and 30 required sizes - nobody is going to maintain that number by hand, and a static text would go stale on the very first change of either side. A computed one cannot go stale by construction.
**Considered and rejected:** - a README with the layout of the upstream icons - it goes stale silently, and silent staleness is exactly the failure the index is written against; - generating a document into the repository in CI - the same stale file, only with a ritual around it.
**When to revisit:** if a consumer appears that needs the index without a fork tree at hand - then a serialized snapshot will be needed, and its staleness will have to be detected explicitly.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-PERMISSIVE-LICENCES:
**Decision:** only MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, MPL-2.0 and Zlib are admissible in the closure of the dependencies; what is checked is a scan of the CLOSURE and not of the top-level package, and its output is recorded in the report.
**Why:** The owner's rule, not open to discussion, and it has already done its work: `sharp` was taken off the table because it pulls in libvips under LGPL. The top level proves nothing: `@resvg/resvg-js` declares MPL-2.0, while the statically linked crates carry BSD-3-Clause (tiny-skia), Apache-2.0 OR MIT (rustybuzz, ttf-parser, roxmltree, svgtypes, simplecss, fontdb, data-url, xmlwriter, png, flate2, serde_json) and Zlib.
**Considered and rejected:** - reading only the `license` field of the top package - it does not see the closure, and the prohibition applies precisely to the closure; - trusting the wording in the package README - not checkable by a third party.
**The owner's clarification of 2026-09-06 - ISC is admissible.** The rule forbids viral copyleft, and ISC is not copyleft at all: it is effectively MIT with two phrases struck out, and the default npm licence. The enumeration of four names was an enumeration and not a closed list. In the closure, ISC is carried by `picocolors` and `siginfo` - transitive dependencies of vitest, that is, of development only; in the runtime closure of `imageset` there is nothing but MPL-2.0.
**When to revisit:** on every change to `npm-shrinkwrap.json` that touches the dependencies of `imageset`; observed through the closure scan, whose output has to lie in the campaign report.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-ROLE-TABLE: Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-006#DECISION-IMAGESET-ROLE-TABLE; the address stays for citations.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-INDEX-NO-LOCK:
**Decision:** `index` does not take the tree lock, unlike `gen`.
**Why:** It opens the same two sources `gen` does and writes neither of them; the worst consequence of a race is a report that is a moment out of date. A lock, meanwhile, would be held for the whole time `gen` runs - minutes of rendering thirty sizes - and reading the report would turn into waiting for a write.
**Considered and rejected:** - taking the same exclusive lock - it serializes a read behind a write of many minutes, for a report that does not have to be transactional anyway; - introducing a shared read lock - locks in codkit are exclusive (PROP-006 §2), and a new class of lock would have to be created for a command that writes nothing.
**When to revisit:** if `index` starts writing anything - a cache, a snapshot, anything at all; then the lock is mandatory.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-WHOLE-BRAND-SURFACE: Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-006#DECISION-IMAGESET-WHOLE-BRAND-SURFACE; the address stays for citations.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-GUARD-PER-FAMILY:
**Decision:** the identifier of the guard test is derived from the family and not from the artwork: `guard.brand.<family>`, five suites for 84 targets.
**Why:** The rule "a new map entry requires a guard test declared beforehand" stays in force without a single exception - only the granularity changes. Nobody would write fifty-five suites for the file-type icons; they would be written as one suite with fifty-five nearly identical bodies or, more likely, the rule would be evaded. A requirement that cannot be met honestly cancels itself, and it is better to notice that in the specification than in somebody's evasion of it.
**Considered and rejected:** - `guard.brand.<artwork>` - 60 suites; the rule turns into a formality filled in by copy-paste; - one common `guard.brand` for everything - it loses what a guard exists for: the installer suite and the file-type-icon suite check different contracts (an opaque background against transparency, one frame against nine); - deriving the guard from the container instead of the family - `icon` lives in five containers at once and their drawing is one; splitting it by container means splitting one contract.
**When to revisit:** if one family ends up holding artworks with different contracts - then the family has stopped being a guard group and has to split.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-ARTWORK-SUBDIR:
**Decision:** the artworks of a family with several drawings live in a subdirectory of the family - `branding/filetype/json.svg`; the flat form `branding/icon.svg` is kept for a family with one drawing.
**Why:** The flat name `filetype-json.svg` would collide in meaning with the already occupied form `<key>-<N>.png`: one and the same hyphen would mean a size in one place and the name of a drawing in another, and the reader of a directory of sixty files could not tell an override from an artwork except by checking whether the tail consists of digits. A subdirectory separates the two meanings syntactically rather than by convention, and it makes the masters directory readable into the bargain: one family, one folder.
**Considered and rejected:** - flat names with a hyphen - the collision of meanings described above; - a separate index file mapping a target to a master - one more document that has to be kept from going stale; the whole command is built on the opposite principle (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-INDEX-IS-COMPUTED`); - a directory for EVERY family, the single ones included - `branding/icon/icon.svg` stutters, and there is no reason to demand a migration of the existing flat masters.
**When to revisit:** if a family with one drawing gains a second one - then its master moves into a subdirectory, and that is the only migration the convention allows.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-VECTOR-PASSTHROUGH:
**Decision:** an SVG target is delivered byte for byte from the vector master; no rendering, no normalization, no rewriting of the document.
**Why:** The application loads these files as vectors and scales them itself. Rasterizing a vector in order to hand a raster to a place that expects a vector is a loss without a gain; normalizing the document (rewriting the paths, cleaning out the attributes) means taking on the responsibility that the drawing did not change after the rewrite, and that can be checked only by rasterization, which is the very thing we wanted to avoid. An empty diff on a repeated regeneration comes free here, because the bytes were never touched.
**Considered and rejected:** - rasterizing to PNG and swapping the reference - it changes how the application loads the resource, that is, it patches upstream code for the sake of a picture; - running it through an SVG optimizer - a new dependency, output that is not deterministic across versions, and the same uncheckability of the result; - not checking the size of the master - a watermark of the wrong size would travel into the product silently, and it would be seen in the layout.
**When to revisit:** if upstream starts assembling these SVGs from a template at build time - then the target stops being a file, and the delivery has to move into a layer that can patch the generator.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-DECLARATION-FILE:
**Decision:** the product declares frame sets and master sources in `imageset.json` in the root of the masters directory, a data file versioned with the masters in the product repository, and not in a section of `codkit.json`.
**Why:** The owner's direction of 2026-09-23 was to teach the generator what a product needs, and to teach it configurably, instead of shipping a container built by hand. The declaration names master keys, so it belongs next to the masters it names: one directory then holds the drawings and the rules for which frame each of them serves, and a second masters directory given with `--branding-dir` carries its own rules instead of borrowing those of another set of drawings. `codkit.json` is the configuration of the whole patch set: every command reads it and its schema belongs to the core, so a malformed image rule there would stop commands that never touch an image, and the core schema would have to learn the vocabulary of one command. The masters directory is already the image set's own place in the product repository, and `##DECISION-IMAGESET-DEFAULT-MASTERS-DIR` kept its path out of `codkit.json` for the same reason.
**Considered and rejected:** - a section of `codkit.json` - the reasons above; - a container built by hand and dropped into the patch set - exactly what the owner did not want: it is regenerated by nobody, and it drifts from the masters at the first new drawing; - flags of `imageset gen` - not versioned, not reviewed, and forgotten on the next run.
**When to revisit:** if a declaration has to span several masters directories, or a command outside the `imageset` namespace has to read it.

p.LICENSE-NAMESPACE: `license` is a namespace (like `imageset`): a bare `codkit license` and an unknown subcommand print the list of subcommands and exit 2 through `usageFail`, before the roots are resolved; it has no `--help` of its own - the command reference answers the question about it. The subcommands: `check`, `annotate`, `notices`.

p.CMD-LICENSE-CHECK: `codkit license check [<dir>]` is the check of the licence markup of a package directory per PROP-014 §3 (`LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM`): the carriers of every file in REUSE precedence order, the own/third-party classification, the `REUSE.toml` registry and the allowlist, orphan sidecars, and the consistency of `vibe.toml`/`LICENSE`/`LICENSES/`/`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. `<dir>` is a path (relative to cwd or absolute); without the argument it is the standards package from toolRoot (PROP-014 `STD-PACKAGE-LOCATION`). No roots are needed (`roots: 'none'`, `configMode: 'none'`): checking a directory does not have to know a patch set. Read-only; git is not called; symbolic links are not resolved. The output is `LIC-CHECK-REPORT`; `--json` is `data: {dir, files, checked, problems, policy}`. Codes: 0 clean; 1 there are problems (`CK-E-LICENSE-HEADER`, `CK-E-LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY`, `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE`); 2 the environment (no directory, a broken policy or SPDX list - `CK-E-CONFIG`, an unreadable file). It is idempotent.

p.CMD-LICENSE-ANNOTATE: `codkit license annotate [--dir <package>] <paths…> [--dry-run] [--year <YYYY>] [--holder <name>] [--third-party --license <SPDX-ID> --source <text>]` places the carrier (PROP-014 §3 `LIC-ANNOTATE`): on an own file a four-line header in the style of its extension, after the prelude, or a sidecar; on a third-party file (`--third-party`, and then `--holder` and `--license` are required) a carrier with the other party's holder and licence plus an annotation appended to the end of `REUSE.toml`. It is idempotent: a file that already carries its markup is `unchanged`. No roots are needed (`roots: 'none'`, `configMode: 'none'`); `maxArgs` is not limited (the paths); the flags `--dir`, `--year`, `--holder`, `--license`, `--source` take values, `--third-party` is boolean, and `--dry-run` is the common one. `--json`: `data: {dir, files: [{path, action: "header"|"sidecar"|"unchanged", kind}], registry: {path, appended}}`. Codes: 0; 1 (a path outside `--dir`, a licence outside the allowlist or not an SPDX one, a holder outside the policy without `--third-party`, `--third-party` without `--holder`/`--license`); 2 (the environment).

p.CMD-LICENSE-NOTICES: `codkit license notices [--dir <package>] [--dry-run]` generates `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` from the registry (PROP-014 §2 `LIC-NOTICES-FILE`, §3 `LIC-NOTICES`): a non-empty registry → the file is written atomically (`written`/`unchanged`); an empty one → there is no file, and an existing one is removed with a printed line (`removed`); `--dry-run` prints the result to stdout without writing. No roots are needed. `--json`: `data: {dir, path, action, rows}`. Codes: 0; 1 (`REUSE.toml` does not parse, or an annotation is incomplete); 2 (the environment).

p.STANDARDS-NAMESPACE: `standards` is a namespace: a bare `codkit standards` and an unknown subcommand give the list of subcommands and exit 2 before the roots are resolved; the subcommands are `load`, `check` and `license`. The first two need patchesDir and `codkit.json` (`configMode: 'load'`; the fork tree is not read, the tree lock is not taken), because the packages delivered are the universal ones plus the ones the patch set's project type names (PROP-014 `STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`), and `license` needs no root at all (`roots: 'none'`); under `--ci` all three are allowed - there is no network. In an agent session over the product repository all three are outside the read-only allowlist of the hook (`load` writes; `check`/`license` are candidates for the allowlist and are deferred) - these are commands of a human or of an orchestrator.

p.CMD-STANDARDS-LOAD: `codkit standards load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` delivers **every shipped package** (`standards`, `agent-skills`; PROP-014 `STD-SHIPPED-PACKAGES`, `STD-LOAD-ALL-PACKAGES`) into the product repository (the algorithm is PROP-014 §5); at the end come the lines `next: vibe install --offline` (after `--upgrade`, `vibe install --offline --force`) and, when a package carries skills, `next: vibe skill install`. `--upgrade` replaces a drifted or outdated copy as a whole (PROP-014 `STD-LOAD-UPGRADE`, `DECISION-STD-MUTABLE-EDITION`). Order: the package in toolRoot → the licence check of the package (a failure is a report, exit 1 and not a single write; there is no bypass flag) → the preconditions of the manifest (`vibe.toml` with `[project]`, without CR) and the classification of the block → the classification of the target `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v<version>/` (`absent` / `identical` / `drift`) → `--dry-run` prints the plan and exits with the same code without writing → the files are written into a temporary directory and renamed → the two copies of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` (the product root and `delta/own/`, PROP-014 §4a) → the manifest block → the block of rows in `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` when the contract exists (PROP-014 §4a `STD-SCRAPE-STATE-MACHINE`; its absence is the information `no-contract`) → the summary with `next: vibe install --offline`, the note about the licences (`STD-LOAD-LICENCE-NOTE`) and the recommendations for the notice file (`STD-LOAD-NOTICE-PRINT`). Side effects: the version directory in the product's `vibevm/vibepacks/` (a byte-for-byte copy), the two copies of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`, the block in `vibe.toml`, the block in an existing `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml`; nothing more - `vibe` is not called, and `vibe.lock` and `vibedeps` are not touched. A repeat is `up to date`, exit 0, with not a byte changed. Codes: 0; 1 (`CK-E-LICENSE-*` of the package; `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` - the installed copy of the package or the copy of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` differs, with the list of `modified`/`extra`/`missing`; `CK-E-CONFIG` - the manifest block or the scrape-contract block is malformed, a package entry or a notice row is outside its own block; `CK-E-CRLF`); 2 (no `vibe.toml`, or no `[project]` in it - `CK-E-CONFIG` with a hint about `vibe init`; no permissions; a corrupted installation - `CK-E-INTERNAL`). `--json`: `data` per PROP-014 `STD-LOAD-STEP-REPORT`.

p.CMD-STANDARDS-CHECK: `codkit standards check` is read-only (PROP-014 §6): the state of the installed copy (`absent`/`identical`/`drift` with the list), the licence check of the copy, the state of both `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copies, the state of the manifest block (`absent`/`current`/`stale`/`malformed`/`entry-outside-block`), the state of the scrape-contract block (`no-contract` is information, not a finding; otherwise the same five states), a warning about a tail after the block, and other versions alongside. Codes: 0 - `identical` plus a clean copy plus `current`; 1 - any finding, each on a line of its own with a code (`CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT`, `CK-E-LICENSE-*`, `CK-E-CONFIG`) and the hint `run codkit standards load`; 2 - the environment. `--json`: `data: {target, license, noticeFiles, manifest, scrape, otherVersions}`.

p.CMD-STANDARDS-LICENSE: `codkit standards license` only prints and needs no root (`roots: 'none'`, `configMode: 'none'`, `maxArgs: 0`, no flags): the full text of the file `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` that `load` places in the two roots of the product; then the recommendations - where the copies live, that nobody edits them, that links to the file are placed by the product owner alone, from the README of the product and from the patch-set intervention in the README of the fork, and where the three licence scopes end; then, verbatim, the two rows of the `vibe scrape` contract (`[[classify]]` delete and `[[assert]]` paths-absent for `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` and `delta/own/LICENSE-CODKIT.md`) - the very rows `standards load` maintains in the product's `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` itself; they are printed for a contract at a non-standard path (`vibe scrape --contract`) and for review (PROP-014 §4a `STD-SCRAPE-CONTRACT-ROWS`); then the ready `[[annotations]]` entry for the product's `REUSE.toml` (`STD-LICENSE-PRINTS-REUSE-ROWS`). The text of the file is printed with a components block computed for patchesDir when one is given (`--patches-dir` or the configuration), and otherwise with an empty block and a note. `--json`: `data: {file: "LICENSE-CODKIT.md", text, recommendations: [...], scrapeContractRows, reuseAnnotation}`. Codes: 0; 2 - the environment only (an unreadable shipped file - `CK-E-INTERNAL`).

p.RUNTIME-NAMESPACE: `runtime` is a namespace modeled on `standards`: a bare `codkit runtime` and an unknown subcommand give the list of subcommands and exit 2 before the roots are resolved; the subcommands are `load` and `check`; both need only patchesDir (`configMode: 'none'`, the tree is not read, the tree lock is not taken); under `--ci` they are allowed - there is no network. In an agent session over the product repository, `load` is outside the read-only allowlist of the hook.

p.CMD-RUNTIME-LOAD: `codkit runtime load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` delivers the runtime library into the product's `delta/own/codkit/` (the algorithm is PROP-015 §4 `RT-LOAD-STEPS`): the source in toolRoot → the licence check of the version directory (a failure is exit 2 and not a single write) → the classification of the target (`absent` / `identical` / `drift`; a `drift` without `--upgrade` is exit 1) → `--dry-run` prints the plan → the write through a temporary directory → the notice copies with the components block (PROP-014 §4a) → the summary with three hints (the graft in the composition root, the `code-import-patterns` block from `LAYERS.md`, `codkit gen feature`). A warning when the product's `pin.tag` is not in `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM`. `--json`: `data: {version, target, state, files:{written, removed}, notice, verifiedUpstream:boolean}`. Codes: 0; 1 - `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT`; 2 - `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE`, `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE`, the environment.

p.CMD-RUNTIME-CHECK: `codkit runtime check` is read-only (PROP-015 `RT-CHECK`): the state of the installed copy (`absent` is the information `runtime not installed`, `identical`, `drift` with the list), the state of both notice copies and `legacy-copy`. Codes: 0 - `identical`, or `absent` while the notice copies are clean; 1 - `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` / `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` (the notice copies) with the hint `run codkit runtime load --upgrade`; 2 - the environment. `--json`: `data: {target:{state, version, paths}, noticeFiles}`.

p.GEN-NAMESPACE: `gen` is a namespace: a bare `codkit gen` and an unknown subcommand give the list of subcommands and exit 2; the subcommands are `feature` and `brand`; both read the patch set's configuration (`configMode: 'load'`), because the skeleton and the graft are the project type's answer and the type is named there (PROP-016 `TYPE-AREA-GENERATORS`); no fork tree is needed. Flags: `--title <text>` (a value), `--setting`, `--cold` (boolean), `--holder`, `--license`, `--year` (values, as for `license annotate`), `--header-style line|block`, `--header-file <path>` (values; PROP-015 `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`).

p.CMD-GEN-FEATURE: `codkit gen feature <id> --title <text> [--setting] [--cold] [--holder …] [--license …] [--year …] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]` is the skeleton of a product feature (PROP-015 §5 `GEN-FEATURE`, `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`, `GEN-TEST-LIVES-WITH-THE-FEATURE`, `GEN-REFUSES-EXISTING`): three files under `delta/own/contrib/<name>/` (the test in the `test/browser/` of the feature), the import line for the composition root and the reminder about the unit. Codes: 0; 1 - `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`; 2 - `CK-E-GEN-ID`, a missing `--title`, incompatible header flags, an unreadable `--header-file`, the environment. `--json`: `data: {id, files:[…], importLine, headerWritten:boolean, headerStyle: "line"|"block"|"file"|null}`.

p.CMD-GEN-BRAND: `codkit gen brand [--holder …] [--license …] [--year …] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]` is the scaffold of the brand table (the header flags are the same as for `gen feature`, PROP-015 `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`) `delta/own/common/brand.ts`, plus the printing of the hook text for `_format` with its reminders (PROP-015 `GEN-BRAND`). Codes: 0; 1 - `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`; 2 - the environment. `--json`: `data: {file, hookText, reminders:[…]}`.

p.CMD-PACKAGE: Build the product's distributable out of the already loaded fork tree. It exists because `ci --profile build` stops at the compile channels and the own tests: until this verb, `build.packageBuild` was a field of the type contract that no module of the engine read, and the last step of a release was a sequence of commands typed by hand whose two ends people got wrong. The order of one run is fixed and is printed before it starts: (0) the inputs the selected targets declare are checked, which only reads and comes first so that an offline run with a missing input is refused before any write (`##CMD-PACKAGE-INPUTS`); (1) the drift guard of `load` - unextracted work is `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE`, exit 1, and the one exemption is the one `load --fresh` makes, a tracked overlay target carrying exactly the strict composition of the configured overlays (PROP-005 §5 `##OVERLAY-KNOWN-MATERIALIZATION`), which a previous `--keep-overlay` run may have left; (2) the overlay targets are materialized into the tree, because a packaged product reads the target file itself and not the dev-channel sidecar; (3) the stamps the type names (`build.packageStamps`) are put into the environment of the commands below, filled from the tree head, the pin or the type's own answer - except a name the operator already exported with a non-empty value, which keeps the operator's value and is printed as `stamp <name>=<value> (from environment)` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-STAMPS-FILL-A-GAP`); (4) the build commands of the selected targets (`##CMD-PACKAGE-TARGETS`) - `build.packageBuild` for a type without a catalog - run in the tree, each command's whole output printed, or in the type's container over the tree for a target on its container route (`##CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER`); (5) then `build.packageDistributable` - the packaging step the patch set declared - runs on the same terms; (6) the existing artifacts matching the outputs of the selected targets and `build.packageOutputs` are printed (`##CMD-PACKAGE-TARGET-OUTPUTS`); (6a) the paths the type names as the residue of its packaging (`build.packageScratch`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH`) are returned to the tip of the loaded tree - only the tracked ones that changed, whatever the verdict of the packaging, and **also under `--keep-overlay`**, which keeps the materialization and never the residue; (7) the overlay targets **this run materialized itself** are returned to the pin and the dev channel is rewritten, exactly as `load --fresh --discard` does for those files - not a fresh pass: build outputs, dependency roots and everything else in the tree are left alone. Step 7 runs whatever the verdict of steps 4-5, so a build that fails halfway never leaves a developer's tree in packaging state. It is not a daemon, so the wrapper of §13 does not apply and `--timeout <seconds>` bounds one command instead of one pass; it holds the per-tree lock like every writing command. Flags: `--keep-overlay` (skip step 7 - never step 6a - for a hand check of the package in the tree; `codkit load --fresh` is the way back), `--skip-type-build` (skip step 4, when the watch channels already built the application), `--timeout <seconds>`, `--inputs <dir>` (the pre-provisioned inputs, `##CMD-PACKAGE-INPUTS`), `--container-prefix <name>` (the first word of the names of the container route, `##CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER`), `--json`. There is deliberately **no `--discard`**: giving up somebody's unextracted work is never a side effect of packaging, and the guard of this command may only be narrowed by codkit's own materialization. Codes: 0; 1 - the guard, or a packaging command that exited non-zero (`CK-E-PACKAGE-FAILED`, naming the label, the exit code and the tail of what the command printed); 2 - the environment (an unusable tree, a command that could not be started at all, a malformed `--timeout`, a target without a route on this host - `CK-E-CONFIG`, an offline run with a missing input - `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN`). `--json`: `data: {steps:[{name,state,detail}], materialized:[…], restored:[…], scratchRestored:[…], stamps:{…}, stampsFromEnvironment:[…], commands:[…], outputs:[…], targets:[…], routes:[…], inputs:[…]}`.

p.CMD-PACKAGE-TARGETS: `codkit package [<selector>]` accepts an exact type-owned target id, a platform family (`windows`, `linux`, `macos`) or `all`. With no selector it uses `typeConfig` through the configured type's `defaultPackageTargets`. Every selected target gets its route on the current host (`##CMD-PACKAGE-HOST-ROUTES`): natively in the tree, in the type's container, or none. A family selector and `all` retain only the targets that have a route on this host; an exact target without one refuses rather than attempting an unproved cross-build. The selected ids and their routes are printed before the plan - `package targets: linux-x64-deb (container), linux-x64-rpm (container)` - and returned as `data.targets` and `data.routes`.

p.CMD-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS-STAY-IN-THE-TREE: Where the artifact lands is the type's answer and the answer is **tree-relative** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-ANSWERS`). A family whose packager writes into a sibling directory of the managed tree therefore names no output at all, and the command says so - `the project type <id> names no package output inside the tree` - instead of printing a path the tool neither manages, guards, nor cleans. This is a refusal to widen the tool's reach, not a gap: the operator reads the location from the packager's own output, which the command printed in full.

p.CMD-PACKAGE-HOST-ROUTES: **Where a target is built is the target's answer, per host.** The host is the operating system codkit runs on - `win32`, `linux` or `darwin`. A target runs **natively** - its build commands in the fork tree, each command's output printed, as every target did before - on a host its `supportedHosts` names; **in its type's container** (`##CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER`) on a host its `container.hosts` names; and it has **no route** on any other host. An exact target without a route is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG`, exit 2, before any write: the message is `package target <id> is not supported on host <host>`, followed by the reason the target gives for it (`hostRefusal.reason`), and the hint is the target's own (`hostRefusal.hint`) or, when it gives none, `run this target on one of: <hosts>` - the hosts of both routes. A family selector or `all` that keeps no target is `CK-E-CONFIG` as before. The plan line of the targets names each route, and `data.routes` is one `{target, route, image, volume}` per selected target in selection order: `route` is `native` or `container`, and the image and the volume are named only for the container route (`null` otherwise).

p.CMD-PACKAGE-TARGET-OUTPUTS: **A target names where its artifacts land.** The `outputs` of a target are path patterns from the tree root, read exactly like `build.packageOutputs` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-ANSWERS`): segment by segment, `*` never crossing a `/`, a trailing `/` naming a directory, and a pattern with an empty, `.` or `..` segment skipped with a warning. The outputs step prints, as `artifact <path>`, the existing matches of the outputs of every selected target in selection order and then those of `build.packageOutputs`, each path once, and returns the same list as `data.outputs`. A target whose packager writes beside the tree names no output, as before (`##CMD-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS-STAY-IN-THE-TREE`), and the step still says so when nothing at all is named.

p.CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER: **The container route builds a target in a container of its type's recipe, and reads the fork tree without writing it.** The recipe is a directory of the type package holding a `Dockerfile` whose entrypoint is the type's entry (`container.recipe`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-TARGETS`); the engine runs Docker and names no tool of a family. One run of the route, in the package build step: (1) the image is `<prefix>-<type>-<platform>-<arch>:<hash>`, where `<prefix>` is `--container-prefix` (default `codkit`; lowercase letters and digits, with single `-` between them) and `<hash>` is the first 12 hex digits of a sha256 over the files of the recipe - each as its path relative to the recipe, a NUL, its bytes, a NUL, in path order - and over the tree arguments; it is built only when `docker image inspect` does not find it, with `docker build --platform linux/<docker arch> --tag <image>` (`amd64` for `x64`, `arm64` for `arm64`, `arm/v7` for `armhf`), a `--build-arg NAME=<value>` for each tree argument (`container.treeArguments`: the first line of the named file of the tree, such as the Node version the tree pins) and a bare `--build-arg NAME` for each variable of `container.buildEnvironment` that the environment codkit runs in carries, so that docker reads the value and codkit never prints it; (2) the volume `<prefix>-<type>-<platform>-<arch>-<treeId>` holds what the container keeps between the runs of one fork tree - its copy of the tree, the dependencies it installed, its caches - and is created when absent; (3) `docker run --rm --name <the volume's name> --platform linux/<docker arch>` mounts the fork tree read-only at `/codkit/tree`, the volume at `/codkit/work`, a directory codkit creates for this one run at `/codkit/io` (`##CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER-PROTOCOL`) and the `--inputs` directory read-only at `/codkit/inputs`, mounts each entry of a provisioned `directory` input read-only at `/codkit/run/<variable>/<entry>`, passes a bare `--env NAME` for each variable of `container.runEnvironment` - a name, or a `prefix*` pattern - that codkit's environment carries, and runs with `--network none` when the run is offline (`##CMD-PACKAGE-INPUTS`); (4) after an exit 0 the existing matches of the target's outputs are removed from the fork tree and every file the entry left in `/codkit/io/out` is copied into the tree at the same relative path, so the tree holds the artifacts of this run and of no earlier one; (5) the directory of the run is removed, whatever the verdict. The drift guard, the overlay materialization, the stamps, the scratch restore and the restore are those of the native route, run on the host around the container, so the container sees the materialized tree. A `docker` that cannot be started is `CK-E-PACKAGE-FAILED`, exit 2, with the hint that the container route needs a Docker engine; an image build or a container that exits non-zero is `CK-E-PACKAGE-FAILED`, exit 1, with the tail of what it printed, and a failed image build names the image and the command that builds it, so that an operator can build it with options of their own - a registry mirror, say - under the same name; a container whose run failed is removed with `docker rm --force`, because one that `--timeout` stopped outlives its docker client. The printed commands and `data.commands` carry the docker commands and never the value of a variable.

p.CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER-PROTOCOL: **What the engine hands the entry of the container, and what it takes back.** The directory `/codkit/io` of one run holds: `commands.json`, the build commands of the target as `[{label, command, args, env}]`, where `env` carries the stamps (`##CMD-PACKAGE` step 3) and the variables of the inputs (`##CMD-PACKAGE-INPUTS`) - the environment discovery of a command (`BuildCommand.environment`) finds tools of the host and is not asked on this route; `outputs.json`, the output patterns of the target; `executables`, the paths git records with the mode 100755 in the tree, and `symlinks`, the path and the target of each path it records with the mode 120000, both NUL-separated - a tree checked out on a host without POSIX modes carries neither, and a bind mount of it shows every file with the mode 0777; `tree-inputs.json`, the provisioned inputs of the kind `tree` as `[{source, target}]`, `source` under `/codkit/inputs` and `target` relative to the tree; `shim/`, the fetch answer, when the run has one; and `out/`, empty. The environment of the container carries `CODKIT_OFFLINE`: `1` for an offline run, `0` otherwise. The entry is the type's (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-004#VSCODE-LINUX-CONTAINER-ENTRY`): it prepares a copy of the tree of its own, places each tree input there where the copy has none, runs the commands of `commands.json` in the copy in order - with `/codkit/io/shim` first on `PATH` when it exists - and stops at the first that fails, copies what the output patterns match to `/codkit/io/out` at the same relative paths, and exits 0 only when every command did.

p.CMD-PACKAGE-INPUTS: **What a build downloads is declared, may be pre-provisioned, and an offline run downloads nothing.** A target declares its inputs, computed from the tree (`inputs(treeDir)`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-TARGETS`): each has a name, the address the build fetches it from, its path inside the inputs directory, and the way the build is pointed at a provisioned copy - `environment`: a variable that names its location - the upstream's own where it has one, otherwise one its type documents - gets the path of the copy; `fetch`: an address the upstream fetches with `curl` on every run, which the fetch answer serves from the copy; `directory`: a variable that names a directory the upstream looks inside - its temporary directory, its cache directory - so the commands get a directory of the run's own under that variable, holding every entry of the copy; `tree`: a cache of the build inside the tree, which the copy replaces. `--inputs <dir>` names the inputs directory; without it nothing is provisioned. The step `inputs` checks the inputs of every selected target before any write - an input is `provisioned` when `<dir>/<path>` exists and `missing` otherwise - and prints one line per input. **The global `--ci` makes the run offline** (`##CLI-GLOBAL-FLAGS`: no network). An offline run with a missing input is `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN`, exit 2, before any write, and its message lists every missing input with where it goes in the inputs directory and the address the build would fetch it from; an online run says `input <name>: not pre-provisioned, the build fetches it from <address>` and goes on. The **fetch answer** is a POSIX `curl` placed first on the `PATH` of the commands: for a provisioned address it writes the copy where `-o` asks, or to its standard output, and for any other address it runs the real `curl` - except in an offline run, where it fails with the address in its message. An offline run points the proxy variables of the native commands (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and their lowercase forms, with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` and an empty `NO_PROXY`) at a closed local port, so that every client that honours them fails instead of fetching, and runs the container route with `--network none`; an image the container route needs and does not find is `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN` too, because building it needs the network. The inputs directory is read, never written. `data.inputs` is one `{name, path, from, state}` per input.

p.DECISION-PACKAGE-CONTAINER-ROUTE:
**Decision:** the engine runs the container route - the image, the volume, the mounts, the protocol files, the copy of the outputs, the offline fence - and the type owns the recipe and the entry that runs inside.
**Why:** A Linux package built on Windows by the native route carried Windows native modules - 19 of the 20 `.node` files of the bundle a Windows host built began with `MZ` on 2026-09-24 - and nothing warned; the remedy is a Linux build over Linux dependencies, which on a host that is not Linux means a container. What the route needs of the host is the same for any family: a read-only view of the tree, a place the container owns, the modes git records, the artifacts copied back, no network when offline. What happens inside - which dependencies, installed how, which directories the copy leaves out - is a family's, and stays in its type (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-ENGINE-IS-BLIND`). The build commands of a target are the same on both routes, so one list of commands is the recipe of a target.
**Considered and rejected:** - the type answering `docker` commands as its build commands - a static command names neither the path of the tree nor the directory of the run, and every type would repeat the mounts, the modes, the copy of the outputs and the offline fence; - building in the bind-mounted tree with a volume over each `node_modules` - the set of those directories is a family's and changes with the tree, and the host tree would get Linux build outputs over its own; - installing the Linux dependencies into the host tree - they would overwrite the host's own, and a Windows tree can hold neither Linux modes nor symbolic links.
**When to revisit:** a family whose container must also run on a Linux host (a foreign architecture), or a runtime other than Docker - observed as a second type that declares a container, or as a Linux host refusing a target that a container could build.

p.CMD-TYPES-XREF: `codkit types` - the contract of the verb lives in `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#CMD-TYPES` and is not restated here: it prints the registered types, their package and version and the capability matrix, needs no patch set and writes nothing.
